metadata.name: Radar Traffic Counts
metadata.description:
Disclaimer: This is a historical dataset (12/16/2017-9/9/2021) that is no longer being updated after September 9, 2021. The Wavetronix radar sensors are being phased out and may not be reporting new data as of 2021.

Traffic count and speed data collected from the several Wavetronix radar sensors deployed by the City of Austin.

The Travel Sensor dataset ( https://data.austintexas.gov/Transportation-and-Mobility/Travel-Sensors/6yd9-yz29 ) is related to this dataset using the 'KITS ID' field. The Travel Sensors dataset provides more information on sensor location and status.

metadata.rowLabel: volume data per intersection per direction in 15 minute bins

columns.name: Row ID
columns.description: A unique ID for each row created as a hash of Row ID, Detector ID, and Intersection name.

columns.name: Detector ID
columns.description: A unique number given to each individual traffic count lane.

columns.name: KITS ID
columns.description: The ID of the wavetronix travel sensor in KITS, the city's Advanced Traffic Management System. This ID is related back to the 'Travel Sensors' dataset which contains further information on device status and location.

columns.name: Read Date
columns.description: The date the data was collected by the radar device.

columns.name: Intersection Name
columns.description: The general location of the sensor. Note: even though the sensor may not be at an intersection, this dataset requires an intersection. For further location information consult the 'Travel Sensors' dataset.

columns.name: Lane
columns.description: The lane that was counted by the device. First two characters indicates direction, NB = Northbound. The last characters explain which lane in that direction. "in" is inside lane, or the lane closest to the center of the road in the direction of travel.

columns.name: Volume
columns.description: The volume, or number of vehicles detected by the sensor, in the last 15 minutes.

columns.name: Speed
columns.description: The average speed of the vehicles that passed by the sensor in the last 15 minutes.

columns.name: Month
columns.description: The numeric month of the data.

columns.name: Day
columns.description: The numeric day of the data.

columns.name: Year
columns.description: The numeric year of the data.

columns.name: Hour
columns.description: The numeric hour of the data.

columns.name: Minute
columns.description: The numeric minute of the data.

columns.name: Day of Week
columns.description: Starting with Sunday is 0 and Monday is 1, and so on.

columns.name: Direction
columns.description: The direction of travel. This information is extracted from the Lane column.

metadata.name: Traffic Count and Data Collection Requests
metadata.description:
This asset is in active development. 

This dataset includes traffic count and data collection requests received and processed by the data collection team at Transportation Engineering Division of Austin Transportation & Public Works.

City of Austin Open Data Terms of Use – https://data.austintexas.gov/stories/s/ranj-cccq

metadata.rowLabel: traffic count and data collection request

columns.name: Traffic Count Request ID
columns.description: The unique identifier as a number.

columns.name: Work Type
columns.description: The work type for the request. The listed work types are: BBANK (Ball Bank), BIKE (Bicycle Count), CD (Conditional Diagram), GAP (Gap Study), PED (Pedestrian), SMADD (Speed Monitor Display Device), SPD (Speed), TMC (Turning Movement Count), VIDEO (Video), and VOL (Volume).

columns.name: Study Type
columns.description: The type of studies done for the request. The listed study types are: All Way Study, BBank, PHB (Pedestrian Hybrid Bacon) Study, Project Evaluation, Radar Gun, SMADD (Speed Trailer), Speed Limit Change, Speed Management Program, TMC (Turning Movement Count), and Speed and Volume.

columns.name: Timeline
columns.description: The timeline of the request. The three types are: Normal, Priority and CAF.

columns.name: Status
columns.description: The status of the request. It will go through the following status listed: Unscheduled, Scheduled, Submitted, Installed, and Completed. The request can be Rescheduled, Cancelled, or put On Hold.

columns.name: Completed Date
columns.description: The date the request was marked as completed in the Transportation Engineering Portal application.

columns.name: Reference Number
columns.description: The reference number either as a CSR number, a CAF, or something else.

columns.name: Work Area
columns.description: The work area of the request. The three work areas are North, South, and Central. This is used for categorizing the request for internal area engineers.

columns.name: Street Segment IDs
columns.description: List of street segment IDs starting with street name and ID.

columns.name: Location Type
columns.description: The type of location as either a specific location, an intersection, or a section of road. The location name format is based on the type.

columns.name: Location Direction of Travel
columns.description: The direction traffic flows for the request.

columns.name: Location Name
columns.description: The location name defined by the primary and secondary street. If it is a long stretch of road, it will list the primary road and define the to and from intersection. Other wise, it will either be an intersection primary/secondary street or it will just be a street address.

columns.name: Location
columns.description: The latitude (Y) and longitude (x) midpoint that the request takes place.

columns.name: Assigned To
columns.description: The type of group assigned to work on this request. It will either be done in-house by the department, or done externally through a contractor.

columns.name: Contractor Queue
columns.description: If the Assigned To is Contractor, the request will be put into a queue. The request contractor queue is formatted by Year number assigned followed by a letter.

columns.name: Created Date
columns.description: The date this request was created in the Transportation Engineering Portal application.

columns.name: Modified Date
columns.description: The date this request was last modified in the Transportation Engineering Portal application.

columns.name: Count of Attachments
columns.description: The total number of active attachments tied to this request.

metadata.name: traffic-volumes-at-intersections-for-all-modes
metadata.title: Traffic Volumes - Multimodal Intersection Turning Movement Counts
metadata.notes:
The City of Toronto's Transportation Services Division collects short-term traffic count data across the City on an ad-hoc basis to support a variety of safety initiatives and projects.

The data available in this repository are a full collection of Turning Movement Counts (TMC) conducted across the City since 1984.

The two most common types of short-term traffic counts are Turning Movement Counts and Speed / Volume / Classification Counts.

*[Speed / Volume / Classification Count data, comprised of vehicle speeds and volumes broken down by vehicle type, can be found here](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/traffic-volumes-midblock-vehicle-speed-volume-and-classification-counts/).*

Turning Movement Counts include the movements of motor vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians through intersections. Counts are captured using video technology. Older counts were conducted manually by field staff.

The City of Toronto uses this data to inform signal timing and infrastructure design.

Each Turning Movement Count is comprised of data collected over 8 non-continuous hours (before September 2023) or over a continuous 14-hour period (September 2023 and after), at a single location. Some key notes about these counts include:

- Motor vehicle volumes are available for movements through the intersection (left-turn, right-turn and through-movement for each leg of the intersection).
- Motor vehicle volumes are further broken down by vehicle type (car, truck, bus).
- Total bicycle volumes approaching the intersection from each direction are available.
- Total pedestrian volumes crossing each leg of the intersection are available.
- Raw data are recorded and aggregated into 15-minute intervals.

The following files showing different views of the data are available:

- **Summary Data (*tmc\_summary\_data*)**: Provides metadata about every TMC available, including information about the count location and count date, as well as summary data about each count (total 8- or 14-hour pedestrian volumes, total 8- or 14-hour vehicle and bicycle volumes for each approach to the intersection, percent of total that are heavy vehicles and a.m. and p.m. peak hour vehicle and bicycle volumes).
- **Most Recent Count Data (*tmc\_most\_recent\_summary\_data*)**: Provides metadata about the most recent TMC available at each location for which a TMC exists, including information about the count location and count date, as well as the summary data provided in the “Summary Data” file (see above).
- **Raw Data (*tmc\_raw\_data\_yyyy\_yyyy*)**: These files—grouped by 5-10 year interval—provide count volumes for cars, trucks, buses, cyclists and pedestrians in 15-minute intervals, for movements through the intersection, for every TMC available. Vehicle volumes are broken down by movement through the intersection (left-turn, right-turn and through-movement, for each approach), cyclist volumes are broken down by leg they enter the intersection and pedestrian volumes are broken down by the leg of the intersection they are counted crossing.

Data dictionaries can be found under each of the views below.

This dataset references the City of [Toronto's Street Centreline](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/toronto-centreline-tcl/) dataset, [Intersection File dataset](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/intersection-file-city-of-toronto/) and [Street Traffic Signal dataset](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/traffic-signals-tabular/).

metadata.name: toronto-centreline-tcl
metadata.title: Toronto Centreline (TCL)
metadata.notes:
The Toronto Centreline is a data set of linear features representing streets/roads, walkways, rivers, railways, highways and administrative boundaries within the City of Toronto. Each line segment is described with a series of attributes including a unique identifier, name, feature code, and address ranges (where applicable).
In addition to retaining historical archives, threaded archives are also retained that record splits and merges of address points, of linear features and of area features. All features are linked and integrated.

metadata.name: Camera Traffic Counts
metadata.description:
Traffic count data collected from the several GRIDSMART optical traffic detectors deployed by the City of Austin.

***This dataset is no longer updated because these devices are no longer maintained***

The Travel Detectors dataset ( https://data.austintexas.gov/Transportation-and-Mobility/Traffic-Detectors/qpuw-8eeb ) is related to this dataset using the 'ATD Device ID' field. The Travel Detectors dataset provides more information on device location and status.


The average speed measurements may not have been calibrated for all intersections. All measurements have been collected using automated machine vision processes and have not been validated.

metadata.rowLabel: Aggregated traffic counts and speeds for a 15-minute interval

columns.name: Record ID
columns.description: A unique ID for each row created as a hash of intersection name, time, truck status, direction, and movement

columns.name: ATD Device ID
columns.description: The ID of the device as noted in the "Traffic Detectors" table

columns.name: Heavy Vehicle

columns.name: Volume
columns.description: The number of vehicles traveling in the respective direction and making the respective turning movement throughout the 15-minute interval

columns.name: Speed Average (Miles Per Hour)
columns.description: Average speed of vehicles that entered the intersection, including those that had started after the end of a red light

columns.name: Speed StdDev
columns.description: Standard deviation of all speed measurements, or 0 if Volume is less than 2.

columns.name: Seconds in Zone Average
columns.description: Average amount of time that vehicles were in the measurement zone, including time that vehicles are stopped at a red light

columns.name: INT_TYPE
columns.description: This field identifies the type of traffic signal•Traffic signal: Signalized system that manages traffic flow at an intersection.•Traffic signal T intersection: Traffic signal installed at a T intersection.•1/2 signal: Traffic signal that manages 2 directions of traffic flow.•1/4 signal:  Traffic signal that manages one full direction of traffic flow and one left turn movement in the opposite direction.•Fire signal: Traffic signal that is activated by emergency services.•Overhead Flasher: Pedestrian activated crossing system consisting of overhead and/or side mounted flashing amber beacons.•Pedestrian RRFB: Pedestrian Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) is a pedestrian activated crossing system consisting of side mounted flashing beacons that flash in an irregular manner.

columns.name: ACCESSIBLE_PEDESTRIAN_SIGNAL
columns.description: This field describes whether or not the signal has audible equipment installed to assist pedestrians with visual impairments

metadata.name: Traffic Counts at Permanent stations
metadata.description: Permanent counts stations are used in trend analysis of traffic patterns around the city.  The stations allow us to create seasonal and weekly variations for traffic data so that we can normalize any portable studies that are of short duration.

limitations: Small source samples and metadata are discovery evidence, not calibrated observations.
Alternative corridors require temporal and approach mapping validation before simulation fitting.
